pointers.sentence: Since 5.1 PostgreSQL's backend, and since 5.2 Oracle's, can take connections from a pool, made by the `pool` property when an alias's `"OPTIONS"` hold `"pool"` (`django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.pool`, `django/db/backends/oracle/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.pool`).

Since 5.1 PostgreSQL's backend, and since 5.2 Oracle's, can take connections from a pool, made by the `pool` property when an alias's `"OPTIONS"` hold `"pool"` (`django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.pool`, `django/db/backends/oracle/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.pool`).

Since 5.1 SQLite's backend takes two keys out of `"OPTIONS"`: `"init_command"`, commands run on every new connection, and `"transaction_mode"`, the mode written after the `"BEGIN"` of an outermost atomic block (`django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.get_connection_params`; [SQLite](../backends/sqlite.md#opening-a-connection-get_connection_params-and-get_new_connection)).

A `"charset"` in `"OPTIONS"` still replaces it (`django/db/backends/mysql/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.get_connection_params`; [MySQL and MariaDB](../backends/mysql.md#the-driver-mysqldb-and-opening-a-connection)).
5.0 added oracledb to Oracle's backend and deprecated cx_Oracle, which 6.0 removed (`django/db/backends/oracle/base.py`; [Oracle](../backends/oracle.md#the-driver-and-the-processs-environment)).
Since 5.0 a `django.db.models.UUIDField` on MariaDB is a `"uuid"` column, where it was `"char(32)"` (`django/db/backends/mysql/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.data_types`).

They say MariaDB 10.7 and later; at this commit MySQL's `DatabaseFeatures.has_native_uuid_field` asks only whether the server is MariaDB (`django/db/backends/mysql/features.py:DatabaseFeatures.has_native_uuid_field`; [Column types: from a field to a column](../backends/column-types.md#mysqls-two-properties)).

Since 5.0 integer fields on SQLite are validated as 64-bit integers, "to match the behavior of sqlite3", the notes say (`django/db/backends/sqlite3/operations.py:DatabaseOperations.integer_field_range`; [The field classes](../models/field-types.md#integers)).
The old function now warns and calls the new one (`django/db/transaction.py:savepoint`; [Transactions: autocommit, `atomic` and savepoints](../connections/atomic.md#savepoints)).

`BuiltinLookup.process_lhs` now asks `lookup_cast` alone (`django/db/models/lookups.py:BuiltinLookup.process_lhs`; [Lookups: `Lookup`, `BuiltinLookup` and the standard comparisons](../expressions/lookups.md#builtinlookup-the-operator-from-the-backends-table)).

Since 6.1 `DurationField.get_db_prep_value` hands a duration to `BaseDatabaseOperations.adapt_durationfield_value`, whose base gives an integer of microseconds (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:DurationField.get_db_prep_value`; [Values in and out: adapters, converters and time zones](../backends/values.md#the-operations-objects-adapters)).

A method under an old name is no longer called (`django/db/backends/base/operations.py:BaseDatabaseOperations.returning_columns`; [Inserts: returned keys, conflicts and batch sizes](../backends/inserts.md#what-comes-back-returning_columns-fetch_returned_rows-and-last_insert_id)).

| `BaseDatabaseFeatures.supports_expression_defaults` | New in 5.0: true by default; where false, `"fields.E011"` refuses any expression but a `Value` as a `db_default` | `django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field._check_db_default` |

| `BaseDatabaseFeatures.supports_default_keyword_in_insert` | New in 5.0, as is `BaseDatabaseFeatures.supports_default_keyword_in_bulk_insert`: true by default; where false, an insert writes a `db_default`'s expression for `"DEFAULT"` | `django/db/models/expressions.py:DatabaseDefault.as_sql` |
| `BaseDatabaseSchemaEditor.sql_delete_column` | Since 6.0, no `"CASCADE"`, which PostgreSQL's editor inherited until then | `django/db/backends/base/schema.py` |

| `BaseDatabaseFeatures.can_return_rows_from_update` | New in 6.0: false by default; where false, an update asked for columns back goes without `"RETURNING"` | `django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLUpdateCompiler.execute_returning_sql` |
| `BaseDatabaseIntrospection.get_relations` | Since 6.1, a third member in each value, the key's delete rule, which inspectdb reads for its `on_delete` | `django/db/backends/base/introspection.py` |
| `BaseDatabaseFeatures.supports_inspectdb` | New in 6.1: true by default; where false, inspectdb raises `CommandError` | `django/core/management/commands/inspectdb.py:Command.handle` |
| `BaseDatabaseOperations.binary_placeholder_sql` | Since 6.1, given the compiler, and returns SQL and parameters | `django/db/backends/base/operations.py` |
| `BaseSpatialOperations.get_geom_placeholder_sql` | Since 6.1, the name of get_geom_placeholder, and returns SQL and parameters | `django/contrib/gis/db/backends/base/operations.py` |
| `BaseDatabaseFeatures.supports_bit_aggregations` | New in 6.1: true by default; where false, a bit aggregate raises `NotSupportedError` | `django/db/models/aggregates.py:BitAggregate.as_sql` |

Since 6.0 too, a keyword argument of a deconstructed call whose name is not an identifier goes into a dictionary after `**` (`django/db/migrations/serializer.py:DeconstructibleSerializer.serialize_deconstructed`).

Since 5.0 a function under `functools.cache` or `functools.lru_cache` is written by its name (`django/db/migrations/serializer.py:FUNCTION_TYPES`; [Serializing values: `serializer_factory` and `deconstruct`](../makemigrations/serializer.md#the-registry-in-its-order)).
Since 6.1 `GenericAliasSerializer` writes a generic alias such as `list[int]` (`django/db/migrations/serializer.py:GenericAliasSerializer`).

Since 5.1 an operation may have a category, `Operation.category`, a member of `OperationCategory`. makemigrations prints a sign before each operation's description, such as `"+"` for an addition (`django/db/migrations/operations/base.py:Operation.formatted_description`; [Operations: the base class and its two halves](../migrations/operations.md#category-describe-and-the-name-fragment)).

Since 5.2 a constraint changed only in what `BaseConstraint.non_db_attrs` names, `"violation_error_code"` and `"violation_error_message"`, becomes an `AlterConstraint`, which changes the state and nothing in the database (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._constraint_should_be_dropped_and_recreated`; [The autodetector: fields, indexes and constraints](../makemigrations/autodetector-fields.md#constraints-create_altered_constraints)).

The autodetector no longer keeps such models apart: a field added to one got no operation under 5.2.17, 6.0.8 and 6.1.1, and now gets an `AddField` (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._detect_changes`).

Such an operation changes the state and no table, since `Operation.allow_migrate_model` refuses an unmanaged model (`django/db/migrations/operations/base.py:Operation.allow_migrate_model`; [The autodetector: comparing two project states](../makemigrations/autodetector.md#detect_changes-the-models-sorted-then-the-generators-in-order)).

The loader follows such a chain down to the migrations that replace nothing (`django/db/migrations/loader.py:MigrationLoader._resolve_replaced_migration_keys`; [Replacing migrations: `replaces`](../migrations/replacing.md#a-replacing-migration-that-is-replaced)).
